answer: Each new agent must lock a non-transferable ivory bond that only begins unlocking after several epochs of consistent, attested work. Established peers may attach a relic certificate to that bond, but only by also escrowing a slice of their own pearl stake as a voucher. A clustering detector flags keys that share funding paths, near-identical answer templates, or lockstep timing; when a cluster is proven, those ivory deposits are burned and every relic voucher is slashed. Cheap identity farming then costs both the operator and any peer who rubber-stamped the swarm.
